question: Does satisfying a traffic signal warrant automatically require installation of a traffic control signal?
model_answer: Direct Answer: No. The MUTCD expressly states that meeting one or more traffic signal warrants does not by itself require signal installation. Warrant satisfaction is only one factor in an engineering study, and the MUTCD even recommends considering alternatives to signals when warrants are met. A parallel rule applies to all-way stop control warrants. Standards (mandatory): - "The satisfaction of a traffic signal warrant or warrants shall not in itself require the installation of a traffic control signal." - Analogously for unsignalized intersections: "The satisfaction of an all-way stop control warrant or warrants shall not in itself require the installation of all-way stop control at an unsignalized intersection." Guidance (recommended): - Because road user delay and the frequency of some crash types are sometimes higher under signal control than under STOP sign control, consideration should be given to providing alternatives to traffic control signals even if one or more signal warrants has been satisfied. - Where a signal is installed based on projected (estimated) volumes, an engineering study should be done within 1 year of putting the signal into steady (stop-and-go) operation to determine if it is justified (except where Warrant 8 was the basis); if not justified, the signal should be taken out of steady operation or removed. Support (context, non-normative): - The safe and efficient movement of all road users is the primary consideration in the engineering study; installing a signal does not necessarily improve safety and could adversely impact safety at an inappropriate location. Warrant satisfaction is one relevant factor in the engineering study, but not the only factor or the overriding consideration. Agencies can also install a signal where no warrants are met, but only after an engineering study documents the rationale. - The Crash Experience warrant conditions are intended for application where crash severity and frequency are the principal reasons to consider installing a signal — illustrating that warrants frame the study rather than mandate installation. Citations: - Section 4C.01 Standard §3 (p.651) - Section 2B.12 Standard §5 (p.79) - Section 4B.03 Guidance §1 (p.649) - Section 4C.01 Guidance §12 (p.652) - Section 4C.01 Support §20 (p.653) - Section 4C.08 Support §1 (p.661)
gold_answer: No. A warrant is a threshold that triggers analysis; it is not conclusive justification. Installation must be based on an engineering study considering safety, operation, alternatives, and the site. A signal can also be installed where no warrant is met if an engineering study documents why it is the best solution.
